notes.title: The store page for the sequel to Dungeon Dev, Debugging Hero, is now live!
notes.notes:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3406850/__Debugging_Hero/

Hello, everyone!

I'm excited to unveil the store page for Debugging Hero, a roguelite action game and the next installment following Dungeon Dev!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/9d76553d169cd958e046d1e255ebcbda33401043.gif[/img]
As the Debugging Hero chosen by the Legendary Sword, you have gained the ability to manipulate character variables!

With your variable manipulation abilities, you can enhance your stats such as attack power and speed.
Not only that, but you can also set a monster's HP to zero for an instant kill or alter its hostility to turn it into an ally.

Use this powerful ability to overcome the dungeons blocking your path and defeat the Demon Lord!

notes.title: Leaderboard Update [2024/11/23]
notes.notes:
Hello!
With today's update, the leaderboard system has been added to Dungeon Dev.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/0ff33b70f0ba92c8caf9ff38ea45fa4e2fcf908f.png[/img]
Now, when you clear a stage, the cost information will be saved to the Steam leaderboard.
You can easily compare your performance with other players using the leaderboard graph and see how your record ranks.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/2f3b2aacda21fbd2f531a0f12b22a29e33f39db4.png[/img]
The leaderboard graph can also be accessed from the map selection screen.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/65024cf4f9e580582520151beb4e7cc8f34a528d.png[/img]
Additionally, you can check the overall records for each stage as well.


Challenge yourself to compete with other players through the leaderboard system and clear maps with even lower costs!

Thank you.

notes.title: Dungeon Dev Update [2024/11/19]
notes.notes:
Hello!
We’ve implemented an update for Dungeon Dev to incorporate the diverse feedback from our players after the game’s release.

Here are the highlights of this update


[h1]Enhanced Cutscene Effects[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/917cc089717fe5856a1b017263ea4ee7a3b20c7b.gif[/img]
We’ve added more dynamic movements to the Demon Lord’s dialogue illustrations, making the cutscenes feel more engaging and lively.



[h1]Stage Success and Failure Effects[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/e2717c969f37893cad5ff486faa70b30a3e40c2d.gif[/img]
To clearly convey the conditions for failure, the Demon Lord will now deliver a brief comment whenever a player meets the failure criteria for a stage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/5802496db855065db5b55639e908a9743f82c650.gif[/img]
Of course, if you successfully design a dungeon, you’ll be met with well-deserved praise from the Demon Lord.



[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where a hero who dies while obtaining a healing potion could remain in a "dead yet targetable" state by monsters.
[*] Resolved an issue where multiple fire traps could overlap incorrectly.
[*] Fixed a bug where stage music would stop when the “Skip Seen Story” option was enabled on certain stages.
[/list]


Thank you!

notes.title: Developer Note: Stage 2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/b5aaae365c021bbf141aac438072687c6b6cf44f.png[/img]
In Stage 2, you'll face heroes from the Royal Knights, whose attack power has been significantly enhanced, alongside new monsters designed to counter them.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/c1dca19e5a128c3f73b6a310b89b1b53668b2f9d.png[/img]
After you successfully completed your first dungeon design, the human king dispatched the Royal Knights to the dungeon. 
Can you design a dungeon that will satisfy the elite Royal Knights of the human kingdom?


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/47c8b45abe563669487a657bf09faf2f04675cd0.png[/img]
The Royal Knight heroes, clad in red armor, have three times the attack power of the standard heroes. 
The first knight you encounter, despite being a "Tank," has stronger attack power than the "Damage Dealer" heroes from previous stages.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/d767cc97163eb68d959e44af0f7a199b1cc4c364.png[/img]
Therefore, instead of matching them with durable monsters, it is more effective to counter them with monsters that have strong attack power, allowing you to quickly satisfy the knight's expectations.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/ba1ebf8aa0613d59236d8c7692508c8136c43c7e.png[/img]
This time, a Royal Knight hero appears alongside a regular hero. If the "Tank" hero deals too much damage, it can interfere with fulfilling the "Damage Dealer" hero’s expectations. 
However, in this map, the only "Tank" hero is from the Royal Knights, and their attack power surpasses that of the regular "Damage Dealer" heroes. Without the right strategy, the "Tank" hero may end up dealing the damage that the "Damage Dealer" heroes need to fulfill their expectations, making it harder for the "Damage Dealers" to succeed.

Here are two strategies the player can utilize:

[list]
[*] Place just enough monsters around the "Tank" hero to barely meet their requirement, while positioning other monsters farther away to limit the damage the "Tank" can deal.
[*] Focus attacks on the "Tank" hero to quickly fulfill their expectations and eliminate them from the battle.
[/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/a5f7a5967a30674ddcf715a2abf26fdba8074521.png[/img]
Next, a "Damage Dealer" swordsman from the Royal Knights makes an appearance. In this map, they appear alongside regular swordsmen.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/e2447ca888308e685a8329b06947870e4a7df9e9.png[/img]
Since the Royal Knight swordsman has even higher attack power based on their already powerful stats, a typical placement strategy will result in the Royal Knight swordsman wiping out all the monsters, making it difficult for the regular swordsmen to deal enough damage. 
You’ll need to strategically place monsters to ensure that the Royal Knight swordsman is defeated after just meeting their damage requirement, allowing the regular swordsmen to also have a chance to deal damage.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/28b8758a291be19e9ad03d0950366e2e944674b5.png[/img]
A good strategy here is to split your monster forces into two groups—use the first group to handle the Royal Knight swordsman appropriately, and then use the second group to deal with the remaining regular swordsmen.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/6ac79fab2c9c51f041e27040aea871a2b8706b09.png[/img]
Midway through the stage, you'll be able to deploy the new monster, the Orc Axe Thrower.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/574c4109eee75bee159eaa69e7a826c072a1a257.gif[/img]
By using the terrain effectively, the Orc Axe Thrower can be a powerful counter to "Tank" heroes.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/94db9d48550fd95fc0308ca52458a7b6df74c628.png[/img]
Finally, you’ll encounter the Royal Knight archers. Like the Royal Knight swordsmen, they serve as "Damage Dealer" heroes. 
While it’s still effective to aim to defeat them at the right moment, since they’re ranged attackers, it might be harder to execute this strategy. 
To counter this, you'll unlock a new monster—the Goblin Thief.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/da492209f19f569f0f8b269bdb53ce8debb2618a.png[/img]
In this map, the Royal Knight archers are placed behind the regular swordsmen. 
While other monsters can’t attack the archers first, the newly unlocked Goblin Thief can be placed near the heroes without any restrictions.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/232deebd8dd4939b9bc976a840bc1117794236ce.png[/img]
This allows you to place the Goblin Thief behind the archers, giving you more strategic options to choose from.

notes.title: Developer Note: Stage 1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/e8c73bd09f0e3ba5b4914929e0e97917228e91a0.png[/img]
The first stage of Dungeon Dev, which is playable in the demo version, serves as the introductory stage where players can learn the basic gameplay.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/d05a8b352719abd97de35c1ed9fe298bac5553e2.png[/img]
The game begins as you, intrigued by a "Dungeon Developer Recruitment Notice" posted by the Demon Lord, visit the Demon Lord's castle. 
You initially expect to design a "dungeon to defeat the heroes," but things turn out a bit differently. 
The Demon Lord has struck a secret deal with the king of the human kingdom, and your task is to create a "dungeon to satisfy the heroes."


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/ce123d77cd883527849d8b94e18484d943eaae97.png[/img]
To create a dungeon that satisfies the heroes, you must meet two conditions:
[list]
[*] The final winner of the battle must be the heroes.
[*] The expectations of each hero based on their role must be fulfilled.
[/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/9241883694c0f4d6e779621fd34639bd9388f543.png[/img]
In the first map, you will face a swordsman who plays the role of a "Damage Dealer." 
A "Damage Dealer" is satisfied by dealing a certain amount of damage in battle, and as indicated by the UI, the swordsman's damage requirement is 200.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/774c763fe78620259248e9d758199aadb954d502.png[/img]
In this map, you can only place goblins with 75 HP, so to satisfy the swordsman, you need to place at least 3 goblins.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/aa690fab63fc0020670942ca5ae453170d6150e3.png[/img]
Now, you've placed 3 goblins in front of the swordsman. Let's see how the battle goes.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/557d6a967a51bd1c89f3c61b86c25bdba56918a5.gif[/img]
Oh no, the swordsman couldn't survive the attacks of the 3 goblins and was defeated.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/96e8486ca445b8626c0715bcd2883e107e8096f5.png[/img]
This time, let's try spacing out the 3 goblins.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/d6854acf8f0162bc314bc8359c392762386a706c.gif[/img]
By spacing them out, each goblin engages the swordsman one by one, allowing the swordsman's expectations to be met, and the battle ends with the heroes' victory. 
As you can see, even with the same number of monsters, the outcome can vary depending on how they are placed.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/33b32f4b65af19a0c4340733e36019bb60fd4143.png[/img]
In the next map, you'll face a knight who plays the role of a "Tank." 
Unlike a "Damage Dealer," a "Tank" is satisfied by taking a certain amount of damage during the battle. 
According to the UI, the knight's damage requirement is 100.

In Dungeon Dev, the attack speed of all heroes and monsters is the same by default. 
However, to prevent battles from being determined by luck due to a 1-frame difference, the heroes' attacks will always land before the monsters'. 
With this in mind, let's calculate the scenario.

The knight's attack power is 10,
The goblin's HP is 75, and its attack power is 5.

The knight will defeat a goblin after 8 attacks, during which the goblin will attack 7 times. If they fight one-on-one, each goblin will deal 35 damage to the knight. So, to satisfy the knight, you'll need 3 goblins.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/b087b71f8e0e0c62ec4349244b269512c768ac33.png[/img]
Let's place 3 goblins spaced out so that they fight the knight one by one. Now, let's see how the battle progresses.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/51582db152b1f5b78495411932f018af2d65d4ba.gif[/img]
As calculated, the knight takes 105 damage, fulfilling their expectations and winning the battle! 
But there's actually a simpler way to clear this.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/ba6b5404ed9b1a47e6a52a9529eacdc7e3e86133.png[/img]
This time, I placed 2 goblins right in front of the knight. Let's see what happens.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/a9f553a5db3a89f494b77329c8173e57151c8625.gif[/img]
Once again, the knight's expectations are met, and they win the battle! 
Depending on how you place the monsters, the number of monsters required can change.

Alright, now that you have a good understanding of the game, let's quickly go over the next maps.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/52d1347dd6642f851fda1c97993a4c5e0b661f0e.png[/img]
In the next map, the swordsman and knight will team up, and the game will get more serious.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/540e626cc79aceb6190e8ac122816640f3c45077.png[/img]
Even when multiple heroes appear, the concept remains the same: satisfy their expectations and design the dungeon so they can win. 
One thing to note is that as long as all victory conditions are met, it doesn't matter if some heroes fall during the battle.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/a37c5b31933675cd4148acaf5910ae84007155f1.png[/img]
After successfully clearing a few maps, you'll unlock new monsters: the Orc Shieldbearer and the Orc Axeman.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/02da38d26f9ed863b3f4098a7ce515aefe7a8f6b.png[/img]
The Orc Shieldbearer, with low attack power but high HP, is well-suited for satisfying "Damage Dealer" heroes. 
On the other hand, the Orc Axeman, with high attack power, is better for fulfilling the expectations of "Tank" heroes.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/2c79ac172ee89cfd56392e1a117f66f47bd43964.png[/img]
As you continue playing with new monsters, you'll encounter a new hero role: the "Healer." 
"Healers" do not have offensive abilities but instead heal all heroes, including themselves, in a wide area, and must heal a certain amount of HP to be satisfied.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/400f137da27baeb6fa949655eac5253af0db491b.png[/img]
To effectively satisfy a "Healer," you'll need to spread out the monsters' attacks across as many heroes as possible so that the "Healer's" area healing can be triggered efficiently.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/0ac0dbea30a0465fcfcc03b0acb764dd1c519812.png[/img]
The final new hero you'll encounter in Stage 1 is the Archer. 
The Archer, like the swordsman, plays the role of a "Damage Dealer" but attacks from a distance and has lower attack power and HP compared to the swordsman.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/c6934ca22c5e86e600e7cfba9ae5f2831543bc4f.png[/img]
Therefore, when the swordsman and archer appear together, you'll need to carefully place the monsters to ensure that the swordsman's high attack power doesn't end up taking the damage meant for the archer.

notes.title: Demo Update [2024/09/16]
notes.notes:
Hello!

We have updated the demo version of Dungeon Dev.
Here are the main updates.


[h2]Character Pathfinding Code Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/8f01edfe88ab6465355fba4f188ab972a1bb8d89.gif[/img]
We’ve enhanced the existing A* algorithm-based 8-direction movement.
Now, if there are no obstacles between the character and the target, diagonal movement will be prioritized.


[h2]Windowed Mode and Story Skip Option[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/b5b64ec9731176e6f1e65a4088c03c0ec5157df6.png[/img]
You can now select fullscreen mode and story skip options from the options menu.
When fullscreen is turned off, the game will be played in windowed mode.
The story skip option will automatically skip the story when replaying cleared stages.


[h2]Resolution Handling Improvements[/h2]

We’ve improved the code for automatic resolution adjustment in both fullscreen and windowed modes.



Thank you!

notes.title: Dungeon Dev is launching on November 15th!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/fe48e95d03760ec0a7195313052dd8f306cfbaf9.png[/img]
Hello!

The development of the final build for the official release of Dungeon Dev is progressing smoothly, and we have officially set the release date for November 15th!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/233580d3b04729b69d181cfa083d4202a1fa68c3.gif[/img]

You can already try out Dungeon Dev through the currently available demo version, but the full version will include even more gimmicks, offering a richer gameplay experience!

We're also improving the game's UI, which will be revealed in the demo update scheduled for tomorrow!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/f3d0e04163336aad1bdf78588b3f3d8adc9c277d.gif[/img]

Don’t forget to add Dungeon Dev to your wishlist and get ready to design special dungeons that will satisfy the kingdom's heroes!

notes.title: Dungeon Dev Demo Update [2024/08/23]
notes.notes:
Hello!

We have updated the demo version of Dungeon Dev.

The main contents of this demo update are as follows:

- Revised gameplay UI
- Added demo content [Playable across 18 maps in Stage 1]
- Sound and language options
- Support for Korean, English, Japanese, and Chinese languages
- Dialogue and font data are available in CSV files to facilitate customization

For languages other than Korean, the translations were done with the help of translation tools, so there may be some awkward phrasing. 
If you could propose any translation improvements on the community hub, we would be grateful and will review them with appreciation.

Regarding the full version, content development is almost complete, and we are currently working on translations. 
After participating in the Steam Next Fest in October, we plan to officially release the game on November 15th.

Thank you!

notes.title: Dungeon Dev Demo release!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44931943/fe48e95d03760ec0a7195313052dd8f306cfbaf9.png[/img]

Hello there!

We are excited to announce the release of the demo version of Dungeon Dev, a game that designs dungeons where is narrowly defeated by the heroes!

Dungeon Dev is inspired by the level design work of game developers, presenting a puzzle game concept where you design dungeons of appropriate difficulty.

While there are still many rough edges, we will continuously update and refine the game to make it more enjoyable.

Thank you for your support!
